statusText: The CME weekend halt still governs this assessment: nothing has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and nothing will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about ten hours past the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail therefore holds at 10% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green - a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than observed extension. What separates this hour from the previous two is that the escalation ledger grew again instead of merely being confirmed. Hezbollah's Naim Qassem said near 13:19 UTC that Israel's strikes "will be met with an appropriate response" and urged Beirut to halt the "humiliating" negotiations, after the deadliest Israeli attack in Lebanon since the June truce killed nine to eleven people in Ansar, Nabatieh and Deir al-Zahrani. Iran separately said Qatar is holding three of its pilots and demanded their release, adding a second Gulf-state friction point. Stress therefore rises one point to 54% (elevated): an explicit retaliation threat is a genuine new leg, and the promised U.S. economic-isolation package still lands inside the coming week. The counterweight is unchanged and equally observed - VIX closed Friday at 14.25, less than a point above its 52-week low of 13.38, and the Nasdaq-100 closed down only 0.13% and about 2.3% below its 52-week high. Confidence is 61% (solid): NQ, VIX, WTI and Brent, both key Treasury maturities and the full seven-day calendar were each re-read directly this hour, and the price evidence is stale by necessity rather than by omission.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. Gap risk remains genuinely two-way. Pulling one way: a Hezbollah retaliation threat that reopens a second front, a U.S. economic-isolation package explicitly promised for next week, a presidential claim of sovereignty over the strait that Tehran has publicly rejected, Iran-Oman reopening talks confirmed as still unresolved, 62 commercial ships redirected by the blockade, a third ADNOC vessel struck in under a week, WTI at $82.40 after a +5% week and +33% year with an IEA deficit warning attached, and a 10Y at 4.696% pressing a 19-month high. Pulling the other: VIX within a point of its 52-week low, an index that closed the week only 0.13% lower after a third consecutive higher week, and a Friday tape that absorbed the escalation with a mid-range settle rather than a liquidation. Treat the reopen as a checkpoint to be scored on observed price path, not as a pre-committed direction. The dated calendar checkpoints begin Monday and culminate in the FOMC minutes on Wednesday; the undated one - the Treasury's Iran package - is deliberately absent from the verified calendar because no exact date has been published.
headline: Hezbollah threatens an "appropriate response" after the deadliest Lebanon strikes since the June truce, lifting Stress to 54%; with CME shut a second day Tail holds at 10% and the action stays EA_ON.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from the primary quote page, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, on 397,964 contracts, with the session settling inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide and no close pinned to either extreme. NQ sits about 2.7% below its 52-week high of 30,975.50 against a 52-week low of 22,961.50. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, about 2.3% below its 52-week high, and the week was the third consecutive higher one. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle, several percent off the highs, is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension and pinning near extremes that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency here is not merely low - it is unmeasurable, because nothing has traded for more than sixteen hours.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close, all re-verified this hour). The split in the evidence remains the central fact of this assessment. Equity volatility is calm to the point of complacency: VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60% on the day, inside a 14.18-14.72 range and only 0.87 points above its 52-week low of 13.38 against a 52-week high of 35.30. Rates and energy say the opposite. The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 4.696%, +5.5bp on the day and at the top of a 4.625-4.700% range, pressing the 52-week high of 4.747% set earlier in the week; the 2-year closed at 4.171%, +3.1bp, inside a 4.098-4.178% range against a 52-week range of 3.365-4.370%. The curve is therefore steepening on long-end inflation aversion rather than signalling a growth scare. WTI settled at $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day, +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and +32.95% on the year; Brent at $88.52, +$1.45 or +1.67%. Trading Economics attributes the move to the U.S. Treasury's unprecedented economic measures against Iran, the continuing naval blockade of Iranian ports, a Houthi strike on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery, and an IEA warning of the widest 2026 global deficit in five years, partly offset by some Middle Eastern crude reaching U.S. markets. Friday's equity weakness was concentrated in semiconductors rather than broad.

GEOPOLITICS (observed, and the only thing moving today). The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed since fighting began in late February; only eight vessels crossed on Monday against a pre-war average of 120, per Kpler. The ledger accumulated over earlier hours is unchanged and unresolved: President Trump said he would declare the strait a territory of the United States, and Iran's Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi rejected the claim near 10:37 UTC; Treasury Secretary Bessent's economic-isolation package is confirmed for next week and paired with a port blockade the Pentagon says it can sustain indefinitely; CENTCOM counts 62 commercial ships redirected; the ADNOC tanker struck Friday evening was the third ADNOC vessel hit in under a week, and the UAE's Anwar Gargash pledged near 12:54 UTC to "safeguard our rights to freedom of navigation … while continuing the path of dialogue". Foreign Minister Araghchi still conditions any reopening on sanctions relief and war reparations, and reporting confirms Iran and Oman have not closed the gap, with market confidence in a deal described as clearly eroding. What is NEW this hour is a second front rather than more of the same. Israeli strikes on Ansar, Nabatieh and Deir al-Zahrani early Saturday killed nine to eleven people including children - the deadliest attack in Lebanon since the June 20 agreements sharply reduced hostilities - and near 13:19 UTC Hezbollah leader Naim Qassem said the attacks "will be met with an appropriate response", asking Beirut "how can you accept this ongoing humiliation of the Lebanese army" and urging it to halt the negotiations. Israel's military says it struck Hezbollah infrastructure in response to action against its soldiers at the Ali al-Taher Ridge; Prime Minister Salam said the civilians killed were "not military targets" and President Aoun called the strikes a "clear message" undermining the U.S.-backed implementation work. Separately, Iran said near 12:48 UTC that Qatar has held three of its pilots since March and demanded their release, opening a second point of friction with a Gulf state.

ASSESSMENT. Tail is held at 10% and stays deep in the low band. Every element the definition asks for - persistent directional efficiency, failed retracements, repeated extension, NQ holding near extremes - is either absent in the last observed session or unobservable in a halted market, and the non-zero level exists to price weekend headline discontinuity that must eventually clear through a gap rather than through intraday structure. That maps to EA_ON and green, and the mapping is mechanical from current Tail alone. Stress rises one point to 54% (elevated) after holding at 53% for an hour. The increment is deliberate and small: an explicit Hezbollah retaliation threat following the deadliest Lebanon strikes since the truce is a new escalation leg, not the corroboration of already-scored threads that the previous hour produced, and it widens the plausible surprise magnitude at Sunday's reopen by adding a front that was quiet a week ago. It is only one point because a threat is not yet an act, because the Lebanon channel has historically transmitted to Nasdaq far more weakly than the Hormuz oil channel, and because the counter-evidence is equally observed and equally fresh: a VIX within a point of its 52-week low and an index down 0.13% on the week's final session do not describe a market braced for a difficult high-volatility environment. The contract is explicit that conflicting signals should raise Stress rather than Tail, and dominantMode is mixed for exactly that reason. Confidence is 61% (solid): NQ futures, VIX, WTI and Brent, both key Treasury maturities, the full seven-day U.S. calendar and the geopolitical wire were each read directly this hour from primary or exchange-quote pages, and the new Lebanon facts are corroborated across three independent outlets. Four news and quote domains returned 403, 451 or 404 to direct fetches this hour and were replaced with alternatives that resolved, so no dimension went unverified. The ceiling on confidence is the structural absence of a live price path - a limitation no provider can escape this weekend - not a gap in what was gathered.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout, so the action was EA_ON and the status green in every available slot. Tail held 7-9% across Friday's U.S. cash session, where the data landed and produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, then printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress traced a clear event arc: 40-44% across Friday afternoon and the U.S. cash session, then easing to 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. From 06:00 UTC the weekend escalation sequence lifted the series steadily - Tail to 10% and Stress through 48%, 50%, 51%, 52% and 53% - as the Mokha barrage, the Lebanon strikes, the ADNOC vessel attack and then the U.S. territorial claim landed one after another with no tape to absorb them; 53% then held into the 12:00 UTC slot when the hour produced corroboration rather than new escalation. Confidence ran 37-61%, weakest in the hours immediately around the weekly close and settling at 57-61% across the weekend halt as each dimension was re-verified hour by hour. The 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August is unavailable because no successful Claude snapshot was published for that hour; those fields are null and no past opinion has been rewritten.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 13:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 12:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly ten hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 10% through the remaining Saturday afternoon and evening slots, ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC as the reopen edges into view and to 12% from midnight across the Sunday slots; those increments reflect accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to hold at 54% through the thin Saturday hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, firm to 55% from 20:00 UTC and to 56% from the early Sunday hours as the unresolved threads converge on the reopen. Confidence drifts from 61% to 56% across the horizon as the last live prints age further without replacement. The material catalyst sits just beyond the horizon: the CME reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which the danger window brackets. Inside the horizon the realistic risks are headline-driven - an actual Hezbollah retaliation following this hour's explicit threat, a further Hormuz vessel strike, an Iranian response to the U.S. territorial claim, an early leak of the promised economic-isolation package, or a breakthrough in the stalled Iran-Oman reopening talks - each of which would move Stress and the expected gap rather than produce observable one-way structure. The first scheduled checkpoint is Monday's Empire State print at 12:30 UTC; the week's highest-impact dated items are Tuesday's housing and industrial production data, the FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 19 August, Thursday's claims and Philadelphia Fed pair, and Friday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Its highest-impact undated item is the Treasury's Iran package, omitted from the calendar because no exact date has been published. Nvidia's results on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium later that week both fall outside this seven-day window.
